title: Classify a case for M&M review
brief:
Your hospital's Morbidity and Mortality (M&M) committee meets monthly to review adverse events. The committee's criteria for mandatory review are: **(1)** unexpected in-hospital death, **(2)** return to theatre within 30 days of a planned procedure, or **(3)** any complication rated as Severe or higher on the WHO ICPS harm scale.

A 58-year-old man underwent elective hernia repair. On day 3 post-operation he developed a surgical-site infection. He was treated with antibiotics and discharged on day 8. No further complications were recorded.

task.stem: Should this case be referred for M&M review?

options.label: Yes — a surgical-site infection is a complication. Classify harm severity first; refer if it meets the Severe threshold.
No — the patient recovered and was discharged; complications that resolve do not meet M&M criteria.
Yes — all post-operative complications are automatically referred for M&M review.
No — M&M review is only for deaths; this patient survived.

debrief.correct: Correct. A surgical-site infection is a complication, so the next step is to classify its harm severity using the WHO ICPS scale (None / Mild / Moderate / Severe / Death). A day-3 SSI treated with antibiotics, resolved by day 8, is most likely Moderate harm — which does not trigger the mandatory Severe threshold. However, you must classify first; you cannot skip the severity step and assume it is below the threshold. If the committee uses a lower threshold (e.g., Moderate and above), the answer changes — always apply your hospital's defined criteria.
debrief.wrong: Recovering does not mean a complication is exempt from review. The criteria are not limited to deaths (option D). Not all complications trigger M&M — only those meeting defined harm thresholds (option C is too broad). Option B skips the severity classification step, which is required before deciding. The correct process is: identify complication → classify severity → apply the committee's threshold criteria → refer if met.
debrief.rule_cited: M&M classification — WHO ICPS harm severity scale; NAHQ HQ Essentials: Peer Review.
